stops.note: originally a sheath or shell-like casing; the sense 'skull cover' seems to come from the idea of a hard outer shell
first recorded in northern English, where Norse settlers had left a deep mark on the dialect, meaning the top of the head or skull
narrowed to the skin and hair of the head; the grim trophy sense arose from colonial-era North American warfare
stops.meaning: the skin covering the top of the head

current_meaning: the skin and hair covering the top of the head
